name: Zechariah

facts.author: Zechariah the son of Berechiah, the son of Iddo (1:1), a prophet and priest who returned from Babylon. He worked alongside Haggai and wrote the whole book.
facts.audience: The Jews who had returned to Jerusalem to rebuild the temple

about: Zechariah began to preach two months after Haggai, in the second year of King Darius (1:1). Like Haggai, he encouraged the people to finish rebuilding the temple, and he called them to return to the LORD so that He would return to them (1:3).

In one night Zechariah saw eight visions: horsemen among the myrtle trees, horns and craftsmen, a man with a measuring line, Joshua the high priest given clean clothes, a golden lampstand and two olive trees, a flying scroll, a woman in a basket, and four chariots. Their message was that God would deal with His people's enemies, cleanse their sin and finish His house, not by human strength but by His Spirit (4:6).

The last chapters look far ahead. Zion's King will come to her, lowly and riding on a donkey (9:9). The shepherd will be sold for thirty pieces of silver (11:12) and struck down (13:7), and the people will look on Him whom they pierced (12:10). In the end the LORD will be King over all the earth (14:9).

themes.title: Return to the LORD
themes.text: God calls His people not to repeat their fathers' sins but to turn to Him with true hearts.

themes.title: By God's Spirit
themes.text: The temple will be finished, not by human strength but by the Spirit of the LORD.

themes.title: The coming King and Shepherd
themes.text: Zechariah speaks more than most prophets of the Messiah: the Branch, the humble King, the pierced Shepherd.

themes.title: The LORD will reign
themes.text: The nations will come to worship in Jerusalem, and the LORD will be King over all the earth.
